title: DC-area forecast: Nice today, then rain from Isaias Saturday night and Sunday
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: Comfortable and mainly bright, with just some high clouds filtering the sunshine at times. Afternoon highs in the mid-70s.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Comfortable and mainly bright, with just some high clouds filtering the sunshine at times. Afternoon highs top out in the mid-70s.

What’s next? Clouds thicken Saturday, though it should stay dry during the day ahead of the remnants of Hurricane Isaias. Showers could begin Saturday night, with periods of rain likely Sunday. Rain wraps up Monday, then sunshine and warmth return Tuesday.

Today’s daily digit — 9/10: Bright skies despite some high clouds, light breezes, low humidity, and highs in the mid-70s. October, you’re doing great. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Friday): Partly to mostly sunny and delightful. Some high clouds filter the sunshine at times, but highs still target the mid-70s with low humidity. Light breezes come from the northwest, especially in the afternoon. Confidence: Medium-High 😎 Nice Day!

Tonight: Partly to mostly cloudy but dry. Lows are near 50 to the mid-50s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Saturday): A mix of sun and clouds early, then increasingly cloudy through the afternoon. It should stay dry during the daylight hours, with light to moderate breezes from the southeast. Highs reach near 70 to the mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Cloudy and turning more humid as the remnants of Isaias approach. Showers could arrive as early as around 9 p.m., or hold off until after midnight. Lows are in the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

Sunday: Periods of rain are likely, but could become more intermittent and spotty during the afternoon into evening. Pockets of thunder and downpours are possible and, if enough warm and unstable air makes it this far north, there could be a brief threat for a weak tornado late in the day or evening. Highs are in the humid 60s to near 70, with gusts near 25 to 30 mph. Rain totals look to range anywhere from around 0.75 to 2 inches. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Sunday night: Occasional showers continue at night, perhaps with a rumble of thunder, before tapering toward dawn. Humid, with lows in the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Low-Medium

A few showers could hang on into Monday (Columbus Day) morning, but we should trend drier and perhaps a bit brighter with time. Highs reach the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium

Sunshine and warmth return Tuesday, with highs in the 70s to near 80. Confidence: Medium

It may turn a bit less warm again by Wednesday and Thursday, though models disagree on how much cooler. Confidence: Low-Medium

DC weather history for October 9

Extreme late-season heat in 2007 pushed temperatures to a record 94 degrees, part of the warmest October on record and a stretch that kept fall feeling like summer.
